lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hi Kenji, it's Luis from the coaching program. Is now still a good time?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, yes, perfect timing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Here's what I had in mind for today, but tell me if you'd rather focus on something else.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How are you doing, really?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hanging in there.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Got it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Where could the bedtime goal fit in your day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, I could walk at the mall, it's air conditioned. I don't want to end up like my dad.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What could you try instead?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I think I can do 20 minutes if it's early. It's just me and my husband now, so it's easier.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Part of you is already moving, and you want to keep that going.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You need to walk every day, no excuses.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Everybody keeps telling me that.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, not really. I kept saying tomorrow, tomorrow.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Some people walk inside the mall early, before the stores open. It's cool and it's flat.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I already told my family about my goal.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Did you try the mall?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, not really.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Just get out there, even when it's hot.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is that something you can do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. My mom is staying with us and I'm taking care of her.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've been taking care of everybody.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why is this important to you right now?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, walking hurts my knees, so why bother.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How would things be different if you kept this up?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Good question.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Did you use the step counter?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I think so.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can you do it in the morning instead?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not yet.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you think 5 days is realistic?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not yet.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So what would you like your goal to be for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: So, I'll try to walk 10 minutes on 5 days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: 5. Maybe 6.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If work gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll keep some fruit cut up in the fridge.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Let me make sure I got it. This week you did it 0 out of 4 days, the hard part was work, and next week you're going to walk 10 minutes on 5 days. Did I miss anything?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. You got it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Perfect.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Talk soon!

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thanks, bye bye.

tags.note: Names mall walking and fear of father's fate
Commits to 20 minutes early; sees easier household
Shows commitment by sharing goal with family
Affirms ability to walk despite caregiving load
Knee pain with walking; reason to stop

flags.reason: 'You need to walk every day, no excuses' is a directive push that triggered pushback at line 15.
Participant said they already told family about the goal (commitment); coach ignored it and asked about the mall.
'Just get out there, even when it's hot' is a directive that ignores the participant's heat/access concern and contradicts line 24 autonomy.
Knee pain with walking was raised as a reason to stop; coach did not explore it or consider a clinician check.

score.summary: Coach covered the full call structure and the participant set a concrete, realistic goal with a backup plan. However, the coach repeatedly used directive language ('no excuses', 'just get out there') and missed change talk and a knee-pain cue, which undermined partnership.
strengths: Line 12 and 27: complex reflection and affirmation captured the participant's effort and ambivalence.
Line 40-45: participant set a specific goal and backup plan, with confidence rating elicited at line 42.
Line 46: clear summary and line 48 set a midweek check-in.
coaching_tips: Line 14 and 22: replace directives with reflection, e.g., 'Walking feels hard right now, and you still want to find a way.'
Line 19: reflect and affirm the commitment ('You've already shared your goal with family') before moving on.
Line 30: explore the knee pain ('Tell me more about what happens with your knees') and suggest checking with the care team.
Line 42: after a 5-6 confidence score, ask what would raise it by one point rather than moving on.
